subject: DPA: proposed incident handoff timelines & subprocessor access (FinServe)

Subject: Urgent — aligning DPA notification windows & subprocessor handoff

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for taking this. We are kicking off an internal review of incident obligations under the DPA and need to align on two items before we proceed with onboarding:

1) Notification window: our legal team expects notification of incidents affecting FinServe data within 48 hours of detection. The DPA language we have references "prompt" notice but doesn't define a clock. Can Redwood confirm the timeline you can commit to for initial notification and for delivery of forensic evidence?

2) Subprocessor handoff: we require the ability to obtain scoped evidence from subprocessors (e.g., GPU operator, storage provider) or an exported artifact in a mutually agreed format. Please confirm your mechanism for evidence transfer and whether you will route through your subprocessors directly to us or provide an export from Redwood.

We appreciate a short summary and any examples of what you can provide (log extracts, exported KV-cache snapshots, chain-of-custody notes). If possible, can you propose a mutual action plan (MAP) so we can sign off on onboarding?

Regards,

FinServe Inc.

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary from Redwood (high level) and then a proposed MAP below.

Initial notification: Our standard is to send an initial incident alert within 24 hours of detection when the incident affects customer data in-scope. We can tighten to 48 hours for initial notice in cases where customers request a contractual floor, but we typically provide a short alert + severity, estimated scope, and immediate mitigation steps within 24 hours.

Forensic evidence handover: We can provide:
- Log extracts (redacted where needed) covering the impacted timeframe;
- Exported artifacts (application-level request logs, pickled KV cache snapshots for model requests) delivered via an authenticated, encrypted SFTP or a secure Share (S3 presigned with short TTL).
- Chain-of-custody manifest for any evidence exported.

Subprocessors: Redwood maintains a roster of subprocessors; we will coordinate a direct transfer if a subprocessor holds primary artifacts (e.g., a managed storage provider). Alternatively, Redwood can produce the export centrally if the customer prefers to avoid third-party engagement. We will also provide redacted POA/chain-of-custody statements from subprocessors where permitted.

Proposed MAP (draft):
- Within 24 hours: initial notification email to FinServe security and legal with known scope and mitigations.
- Within 72 hours: preliminary evidence package (log extracts + manifest) delivered to an agreed secure location; if a subprocessor needs to be involved, notify FinServe of subprocessor name and ETA for evidence.
- Within 7 business days: full evidence handover and technical debrief call (if requested).

We can attach the incident_evidence_checklist we use operationally — see attachment. Ben (copied) will add technical detail on formats and SFTP options. Marissa will follow up on contract language for a narrow addendum that clarifies the timelines and transfer method.

Would you like a 30-minute sync tomorrow to finalize the MAP?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Platform Trust & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Howard <security@finserve.com>

Grace / Ben — quick technical clarifications from FinServe SecOps: 

1) The 72-hour preliminary evidence window is acceptable as long as the initial notice goes out within 48 hours. Our risk team needs the alert early to start containment for downstream systems.

2) Evidence format: preferred is compressed JSONL log exports with UTC timestamps (millisecond precision) + accompanying manifest. If you provide pickled or binary snapshots (e.g., KV-cache), we need a schema and instructions to interpret/extract.

3) Chain-of-custody: we need a signed manifest from any third-party subprocessors that actually host or extract artifacts. If Redwood will act as the single point of contact and produce centralized exports, that would simplify our legal review; otherwise, provide contact + SLAs for each subprocessors' evidence delivery.

4) Transfer method: SFTP or presigned S3 is OK. If S3 presigned, ensure TTLs are at least 24 hours and that links are single-use. We will not accept email attachments for bulk artifacts.

If you can draft the MAP and the minimal addendum language for the DPA (bullet points), that will speed sign-off.

Thanks,
Marcus Howard
Head of SecOps, FinServe
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: security@finserve.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, asha.patel@finserve.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 13:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent — aligning DPA notification windows & subprocessor handoff

Marcus / Asha — technical follow-up and what we can commit to from an ops perspective.

- Initial alert: 24-hour capability for Redwood to send a concise incident notice including detection timestamp, preliminary scope, impacted customer IDs, and immediate containment steps. That notice will be sent to the FinServe addresses on the thread.

- Evidence packaging: We will provide a preliminary package (JSONL logs + manifest) within 72 hours as Grace proposed. The JSONL will include: request_id, timestamp_utc, model_id, route, tokenized_length, and error_code (if applicable). We will also include a mapping file (CSV) for request IDs to higher-level customer identifiers where permitted.

- Binary artifacts: for KV-cache or model snapshots we produce an export (tar.gz) with a README that describes the serialization format and a utility script to deserialize. If a subprocessor must be contacted directly, we will provide a signed statement of the items held and an expected ETA for release.

- Transfer: preferred flow is Redwood-managed S3 export with presigned URL (24h single-use). For customers that require inbound SFTP, we can push to the customer's endpoint under a short-term credential.

- Chain-of-custody: we will include a signed manifest (GPG-signed) for each artifact and log the export job ID in our audit system. We can also provide a redacted subprocessor manifest if the subprocessor's contract allows.

I've attached our current subprocessor roster (redwood_subprocessor_roster_v3.csv) — this is the operational list and includes contact points for those subprocessors. We are open to a narrow DPA addendum that enumerates the 24/72/7b timelines and the transfer method options. Marissa, can you draft the addendum bullets?

Ben
Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

Asha / Marcus — thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Attached is a draft DPA addendum (dpa-addendum-draft.docx) and a short MAP we propose. Key bullets from the addendum: 

• Initial notification: Redwood will issue an initial incident alert within 24 hours of detection to the customer's legal and security contacts.
• Preliminary evidence: Redwood will deliver a preliminary evidence package (JSONL logs + manifest) within 72 hours to an agreed secure endpoint (S3 presigned or SFTP).
• Full handover and debrief: within 7 business days, Redwood will complete evidence transfer and provide a technical debrief (remote).
• Subprocessor coordination: Redwood will act as primary coordinator; where subprocessors hold uniquely required artifacts, Redwood will facilitate direct transfer and provide signed chain-of-custody manifest(s).
• Formats and TTLs: JSONL preferred for logs (UTC, ms). S3 presigned links single-use with 24h TTL or SFTP push per customer's spec.

Next steps: please review the attached addendum and MAP. If it's acceptable, we can prepare a redlined version for your counsel and schedule a 30-minute call to finalize the mechanics.

If you need the MAP to specifically call out any subprocessors by name for FinServe review, tell us which ones and we'll include them in the redline.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
